authoring.value:
Find the volume of the solid $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{2-{x}^{2}},\,0\le y\le 2z}.
$$

Interpret the unchanged inequalities in real coordinates. The square root requires $2-x^2\ge0$, so the actual nonempty $x$ projection is $[-\sqrt2,\sqrt2]$. Find the volume using this real domain.

authoring.value:
The inequalities defining $R$ are retained exactly. In real coordinates, $\sqrt{2-x^2}$ is defined only for $|x|\le\sqrt2$. These values also satisfy the printed nominal bound $-2\le x\le2$. Thus the actual real solid is equivalently

$$R=\{(x,y,z):-\sqrt2\le x\le\sqrt2,\ 0\le z\le\sqrt{2-x^2},\ 0\le y\le2z\}.$$

Its volume is

$$\begin{aligned}
V&=\int_{-\sqrt2}^{\sqrt2}\int_0^{\sqrt{2-x^2}}\int_0^{2z}1\,dy\,dz\,dx\\
&=\int_{-\sqrt2}^{\sqrt2}\int_0^{\sqrt{2-x^2}}2z\,dz\,dx\\
&=\int_{-\sqrt2}^{\sqrt2}(2-x^2)\,dx
=\left[2x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-\sqrt2}^{\sqrt2}
=\frac{8\sqrt2}{3}.
\end{aligned}$$

The original source accepted $8/3$. That value is the ordinary signed polynomial integral $\int_{-2}^{2}(2-x^2)\,dx$. It does not give the volume of this real solid: the source square-root bounds are undefined for $\sqrt2<|x|\le2$. All five original choices are retained as alternatives, and $8\sqrt2/3$ is added as the correct study answer.
